{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABc6lv2g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhGcvC8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 136, "title": "Move browser emulation off the UI thread and decouple audio playback from frame rendering", "body": "## Problem

A maintainer can now launch a locally held PC-98 DOS adventure game in the browser. Scene transitions feel disproportionately slow and background music is not playing consistently. We first inspected the current code and identified a **structural coupling** to fix **before** pursuing fine-grained CPU/render/FM micro-optimizations or doing a performance-profiling project.

Today, [`web/app.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/app.js) runs the following **on the browser main/UI thread** within `requestAnimationFrame`:

```js
for (let i = 0; i < slices; i++) { core.step(16667); playAudio(); }
render();
```

- `core.step` synchronously executes guest CPU, emulated IDE/FDD and all device clocks. [`src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/lib.rs) executes up to 100,000 instruction slots per call and advances devices/audio in the same core.
- `render` synchronously calls `core.frame()` (a full 640x400 raster in [`src/bus.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/bus.rs)), creates an RGBA view and calls `CanvasRenderingContext2D.putImageData` every animation tick.
- `playAudio` copies generated PCM into a fresh `AudioBuffer` and creates/schedules another `AudioBufferSourceNode` per batch, tied to the same main-thread animation tick.
- `AudioContext` is resumed on a user gesture, and playback happens in Web Audio; however **PCM delivery / buffer scheduling remains dependent on frame callbacks**. A busy scene transition can delay input, display, control handling and audio production/queuing together.
- Guest time advances at a project-specific deterministic 8 MHz virtual clock, not real Ap i486DX2 66 MHz. Merely turning up instruction budgets or multiplying by wall time is not guaranteed to help and must not silently alter guest audio/IRQ timing.

This Issue is about implementing the **obvious concurrency/ownership architecture first**, **not** profiling every instruction, optimizing individual FM operators, reimplementing GDC drawing, or guaranteeing arbitrary game's frame rate. A code-level architectural explanation is sufficient to proceed; **do not make benchmark collection or a mandatory before/after performance report a precondition**.

## Expected outcome

Restructure the default browser runtime to keep **CPU+all emulated devices+guest-clocked FM/PCM/IDE/FDD in a single owner on a dedicated Web Worker**, with the browser **main thread responsible for DOM/input/UI/Canvas display only**, and **AudioWorklet handling low-latency consumption of a bounded audio queue**. Video delivery must be asynchronous and coalesced so a slow renderer does not block emulation or build an unlimited backlog. Preserve one authoritative guest-time clock and deterministic order of I/O, IRQs, CPU effects and media writes.

Recommended architecture (the worker/core owns the state; choose the simplest viable message transfer mechanisms):

```
DOM / keyboard / mouse / controls  ── commands ──► emulation Worker
      main thread                                 Rust/Wasm Machine owner
Canvas ◄── newest transferable frame ──────────── CPU + bus + virtual clock
AudioContext + AudioWorklet ◄── bounded PCM ───── audio output from emulated cycles
```

The audio **sample synthesis** remains in the guest-clocked core unless evidence justifies splitting it: AudioWorklet should perform **audio delivery**, not run the guest CPU or maintain its own divergent guest clock. Do not put blocking Wasm emulation in the AudioWorklet real-time callback. An `AudioWorkletProcessor` can accept PCM blocks over a `MessagePort` with a fixed-capacity queue; an equivalent low-overhead browser-supported approach is fine. Prefer transferable `ArrayBuffer`s and bounded buffer reuse over whole-Wasm-memory copies; **do not require cross-origin isolation / SharedArrayBuffer / Wasm threads** merely to implement a single Wasm Worker.

## Implementation scope

1. **Single-owner Worker:** Instantiate the existing production release `core.wasm` inside a dedicated browser Web Worker; all Wasm calls and exported memory views belong to that Worker. Keep Rust headless/native APIs and the original deterministic Machine semantics. Design an explicit small message protocol for media mount/eject, boot source/profile selection, reset/pause/resume, keyboard/mouse, sound-related state and diagnostics. DOM code must not block on synchronous Wasm execution, spin in busy-waits, or share mutable `Machine` access across threads.
2. **Independent, bounded execution scheduling:** Advance guest CPU/devices in finite Worker slices, yielding to queued control/media messages and responding to pause/reset/eject with well-defined ordering. Do not make guest progress contingent on a `requestAnimationFrame` callback, page rendering, or user clicking the canvas. Avoid an unbounded `setInterval` backlog, unbounded catch-up after tab suspension, or a busy-loop that starves worker messages or the browser. Keep guest clock, PIT/OPN/PCM and IRQ semantics coherent. Background tab/visibility behavior should be explicit and preserve the existing safe pause policy or a documented equivalent.
3. **Asynchronous, coalesced frame transport:** Obtain the actual `core.frame()` output from the Worker and send transferable immutable RGBA frame snapshots (or another simple browser-supported frame transport) to the main-thread Canvas. Limit frames in flight (e.g. newest-only with explicit consumer acknowledgement and recycled buffers) and skip obsolete presentation frames. Do **not** transfer Wasm linear memory or schedule a separate 1 MiB+ allocation/copy every CPU slice. A user should still see correct 640x400 text, Japanese glyphs, GRCG/EGC/PEGC bitmap and cursor/blink updates while the worker runs. No requirement for a complete dirty-rectangle cache, GPU renderer or OffscreenCanvas if coalesced frames suffice.
4. **Separate reliable audio delivery:** Replace animation-tick-based `AudioBufferSourceNode` creation with a self-contained `AudioWorklet` playback path and a bounded PCM queue (or convincingly equivalent continuously fed sink). Feed it guest-generated 48 kHz samples at a controlled cadence, with no pitch/tempo changes from batching, and no dependence on Canvas/rAF. Clearly define underflow, overflow, mute/pause/resume/reset, autoplay permission, AudioContext interruptions and device/sample-rate behavior; bounded silence on underflow is acceptable but **never let queued old samples play after reset**, duplicate segments or grow latency without limit. Use original audio code; no third-party emulator/audio synthesizer source.
5. **Asynchronous media and no data loss:** The currently bundled 128 MiB sparse, bootable FreeDOS(98) HDD with HimemX/`DOS=HIGH` must still start automatically and support FDD1/FDD2 live insertion. Route chunked large HDI import/export through the Worker using bounded transferable chunks without exposing whole HDI in main-thread RAM or corrupting a running guest. Maintain the user confirmation on destructive dirty-HDD replacement, accurate `Insert into` vs `Boot from` separation, transactional import/export, readable progress/failures, and reimport of guest-written HDI/floppy bytes. Operations that need a guest-consistent snapshot must coordinate pause/commit at a defined Worker boundary; do not clone the full disk as a shortcut.
6. **Input and UX state:** Preserve physical and virtual keyboard, mouse, focus/blur/visibility key release, `Enable sound` gesture, demo buttons, status/error panels, profiles, reset, pause, boot and media control behavior. Keep the UI responsive while CPU/disk/audio work happens elsewhere, including nonblocking status and startup progress. Prevent races from rapid double-clicks, repeated profile toggles, startup import and stale Worker replies after reset. Handle Worker faults or failed asset/worklet loads visibly without silently claiming successful boot.
7. **Packaging/security and compatibility:** Update `web/` assets, build, base URL handling and strict [site-asset audit](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/README.md#reproduce-the-checks) for the Worker and AudioWorklet entry points; both `/` and `/pc98-rust/` must load assets from correct paths. No remote scripts, game/ROM/font dumps, new unreviewed licensing obligations, service dependencies or cross-origin-isolation requirement. Keep GitHub Pages static hosting supported.
8. **Test interface migration:** Existing Chromium tests use synchronous `window.pc98.core`, `pc98.read`, `pc98.stats`, and direct Wasm stepping/peeks. A Worker move invalidates those assumptions. Provide a narrowly scoped **async diagnostic/RPC test adapter** (or equivalent bounded test harness) that observes the **same Worker-owned real Wasm core**; update tests so they do not mock DOS/device behavior, accidentally keep a second main-thread emulator or bypass the production runtime. Preserve native/headless sync test API separately. Order/ack requests so tests can sample consistent state and wait for actual guest completion rather than racing requestAnimationFrame.
9. **No unrelated micro-optimization:** This issue does not demand a profiler UI, benchmark gate, extensive dirty-region engine, hardware cycle-perfect tuning, rewriting FM synth algorithms, adding sample ROMs, new unsupported PC-98 peripherals, or game-specific fixes. Changes should be a cohesive, minimal threading/dataflow refactor with correctness tests.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Production `core.wasm` runs **only in the dedicated emulation Worker** during ordinary browser play; UI rAF never calls `core.step` or `core.frame`, and no CPU/firmware/IDE/FDD/FM synth executes synchronously on the DOM thread. Main thread continues to handle input, presentation and UI. Guest I/O remains serial and deterministic in the Worker. Demonstrate these properties with direct code inspection and browser tests, **not profiling metrics**.
- [ ] Main thread visibly remains responsive during a sustained **independent, rights-cleared** guest animation, bulk video/VRAM updates or DOS read/graphics sequence; guest progresses without rAF-driven stepping. Use event/DOM responsiveness assertions and guest-result checks, not an arbitrary FPS or speedup threshold.
- [ ] Audio uses a continuously operating **AudioWorklet or equivalent independent playback sink** fed by a bounded worker-to-output queue, not per-animation-frame `AudioBufferSourceNode` scheduling. Verify PCM continuity/order, finite queue and acceptable underflow/overflow policy, reset flush and first-after-reset sample, mute/unmute, pause/resume, permission activation, and no stale queued playback. Play original BEEP plus licensed FM/SSG and 86 PCM guest tests with actual browser audio, not fabricated PC-98 audio.
- [ ] Frame pipeline is asynchronous, bounded/coalesced, handles screen contents changing during rendering, doesn't accumulate obsolete video frames and still shows real pixels/text at the correct geometry. Exercise both graphics and text/cursor changes on Ap and VM, cold boot and reset, including scenes with audio active. Frame transfer is safe across Wasm memory growth.
- [ ] Auto-booted GPL FreeDOS(98)+HimemX remains responsive (`A:\>`, `MEMSIZE` target as before), and both original demo disks still work. Verify actual guest CPU/device behavior, FDD1/FDD2 hot media, keyboard/mouse IRQs, sound, BIOS CRT/KCG changes from [Issue #134](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/issues/134), IDE/HDD read/write and boot source selection. Preserve BIOS/CPU/memory correctness, no partial execution during snapshots or media swaps.
- [ ] Test pause/resume, reset and profile/boot selection with in-flight frame/audio/media requests, including visibility change, Worker failure and invalid media; stale asynchronous replies must not resurrect old machine state, cause stuck input, replay audio or lose dirty disk writes. Users retain a recoverable error path.
- [ ] Chunked large-HDI (including representative **512 MiB/1 GiB** validations where already covered) and built-in sparse 128 MiB disk remain bounded in JS/Wasm memory, faithfully export guest writes and round-trip identical unmodified data. Preserve explicit dirty-HDD discard warning and failure-safe media replacement. Use existing large-disk tests where practical; do not add redundant giant files/runs.
- [ ] Update production **release-Wasm Chromium** tests and their async inspection adapter on both site roots (`/`, `/pc98-rust/`), plus suitable original native tests if Rust core changes are required. No fake Worker-only success, test-only main-thread CPU, private games, physical-hardware or human gameplay as pre-merge requirements. Keep existing applicable acceptance behaviors covered.
- [ ] Build/package Worker and AudioWorklet scripts from **first-party original** code, update approved public asset list and path checks, run relevant fixture/license preparation, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, production Wasm build and appropriate full two-root Chromium suite. Follow [development-flow performance principles](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md#test-and-ci-performance-principles) when avoiding redundant heavy scenarios.
- [ ] No **mandatory baseline profiling, benchmark collection, frame-time instrumentation, FPS target or claimed speedup**. Report **observable structural changes and functional acceptance**; a later task may profile remaining CPU/FM/GDC hotspots. Do not assert a particular game now runs fast or all its music is supported unless independently observed.

## Optional validation

Observe a legally held private PC-98 DOS adventure game's scene transitions and BGM in a local environment after the architectural change, without sharing game image/code/screenshots/audio or other copyrighted content. This can guide later focused optimization tasks, but is **not required for review/merge**.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Live Pages and human/private-game validation are not pre-merge gates; track separate operational issues if needed.
